title: Approval Policy Language & Immutable Audit Logs — PRD sketch
content:
Context:
We frequently get requests from large regulated customers who need:
- machine-verifiable approval gates for network changes (customer-managed firewall/VPC edits)
- audit logs that are tamper-evident and can be retained/exported to customer SIEMs
- a way to bundle approvals + attestations for on-prem handovers during audits

This doc sketches a combined approach: 1) a small domain-specific approval policy language (APL) that expresses gating logic, and 2) immutable audit log anchors (signed log segments + retention lifecycle) so customers and auditors can validate change histories without relying solely on transfer of trust.

Problem statement (short):
Current private-deploy audit solutions are brittle: text logs + exported CSVs are easy to alter, approval workflows are opaque, and customers ask for cryptographic proof-of-change for compliance. We need a reproducible, low-friction way for customers to: enforce programmable approval gates, verify the chain-of-approval after the fact, and archive signed audit bundles that can be independently validated.

Goals (MVP):
- Define a minimal Approval Policy Language (APL v0) supporting rule composition, required approvers, TTLed approvals, and conditional gates based on traffic/impact.
- Implement a lightweight "certifier" service that: 1) validates policy evaluation decisions, 2) emits an immutable signed audit segment per change (JSON-LD record + SHA256 + RSA/ECDSA signature).
- Provide export formats: signed-bundle.tar.gz and streaming append-only protobufs for long-term retention to customer S3/MinIO or SIEM ingestion.
- Add a simple UI in Console for viewing policy evaluation traces and for downloading signed bundles.

Non-goals (MVP):
- Full formal verification of APL.
- Replacing customer HSM/KMS integrations in first iteration (we will support customers injecting public keys for verification later).

User stories:
- Security engineer: "I want to express that any inbound network change touching west-prod must have at least 2 reviewers from the infra-team and an automated risk score under 5 before merge."
- Compliance officer: "During an audit, I need to produce a cryptographically-signed history of network changes for Q4 with proof that approval policies were followed."
- SRE: "I need a quick way to see the policy trace for a rollback we did yesterday (who signed off, why the policy allowed it)."

APL v0 (sketch):
- Syntax: YAML/JSON friendly; small set of primitives: require(roles, count), condition(expr), ttl(hours), policy-when(path|label), deny/allow default.
- Example:
  - id: "west-prod-net-change"
    when: "resource.path =~ '/clusters/west-prod/**'"
    require: { roles: ["infra-review"], count: 2 }
    condition: "risk_score < 5"
    ttl: 72
- Evaluation returns: decision, matched-rules, approver-ids, evaluation-timestamp, risk-metrics.

Audit log model (immutable segments):
- Each change event produces an AuditSegment object (single-line JSON) with fields: segment_id, prev_anchor_hash, change_payload (diff), policy_id, evaluation_trace, approver_signatures (base64), timestamp, signer_key_id.
- Signature scheme: default ECDSA P-256 over canonical JSON bytes + segment_id.
- Anchor chaining: segments include prev_anchor_hash to create an append-only chain. Periodic anchors can be anchored to customer-provided KMS or a Redwood notarization key (opt-in).
- Retention: segments are logically immutable; we implement a retention lifecycle that marks segments as archived and exports signed-bundles to customer storage after N days.

Operational flows:
1) Change-request created (API / Console) -> policy evaluated by APL engine -> if allow, create pre-signed approval token -> approvers sign (Console or API) -> certifier validates signatures -> emits signed AuditSegment -> scheduling of change execution.
2) Bulk export for audits: generate signed-bundle for date range, include segment chain proof, and an index file with verification instructions and public keys.

Console UX (rough):
- Policy editor: small text area with APL linting + examples.
- Change detail: timeline view with policy evaluation steps, approver badges, signature status, hash anchor. "Download signed bundle" CTA.
- Verification helper: UI shows how to run a local verifier (open-source script) that checks chain integrity and signatures.

APIs: (high level)
- POST /apl/validate -> returns trace
- POST /changes -> create change & return change_id, expected_policy_id
- POST /changes/{id}/sign -> attach approver signature
- GET /audit/{range}/bundle -> stream signed bundle

Security & crypto considerations:
- Key management: Redwood holds default notarization key (opt-in). Customers can upload verification public keys.
- We must build a verification SDK (python + go) for auditors. Keep crypto primitives minimal and standard (ECDSA, SHA-256).
- Protect private keys: Redwood never stores customer private keys; signing occurs client-side or via customer KMS (future).

Non-functional requirements:
- Latency: policy evaluation < 200ms median for simple rules.
- Throughput: certifier must handle bursts up to 2000 changes/min in Dedicated clusters.
- Storage: signed segments appended to an append-only store with immutability guarantees (S3 Object Locks or write-once blob store).
- Replayability: verifier must be able to re-run policy evaluation deterministically given stored change_payload + policy snapshot.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (prototype): APL v0 evaluator + certifier in dev, basic console views, CLI verifier. (4–6 weeks)
- Phase 1 (pilot): Selected enterprise customers (2–3) in Dedicated mode, export bundles to customer S3. Add retention policies and small-scale crypto review. (8–12 weeks)
- Phase 2 (GA): support for integration with customer KMS, notarization service, scale improvements, and detailed RBAC. (Q3 target)

Open questions / risks:
- Should we define a binary/compact segment format for very high-volume customers (cost/storage tradeoff)?
- Legal: will a Redwood-signed anchor be accepted by auditors in target verticals? Need legal + compliance sign-off.
- Do we mandate customer-provided public keys for verification or accept Redwood notarization as default?
- Interaction with existing log export paths (SIEM connectors) — avoid duplicating data egress costs.

Dependencies / owners:
- APL engine: eng-servicing-runtime (owner: Marcus Li)
- Certifier + signing stack: eng-infrastructure (owner: Ethan Kim)
- Console UI: eng-console-and-tooling (owner: Sofia Gomez)
- Security review: security-and-compliance (contact: Priya Raman)

Next steps / immediate TODOs:
- Draft minimal APL grammar and publish to Confluence (owner: Aisha) - due 2024-02-19
- Spike: implement certifier prototype that signs a synthetic change and outputs a bundle (owner: Marcus) - due 2024-02-26
- Slack thread: #priv-deploy-audit (create and ping stakeholders)
- Create Jira epic PRIV-402 and link prototypes/PRs.

Notes to self / informal:
- Keep the first iteration simple: humans + signatures + chain = most auditor needs.
- Avoid building an expensive global notarization service before we know demand.
- Consider providing a turnkey verifier container for auditors to run locally during compliance reviews.
